_comment: Fates (fe14) screen and speed extras, our own patches found in this game's code (docs/EXTRAS.md).
Read by tools/extras/usa_extras.py (native entries: tools/extras/native.py). Every site is checked against
extracted/code.bin before a cheat file is written: the function that holds it (config/functions.csv), the
instruction shape of every original word (regex on objdump text), the SHA-1 of the original bytes, and the
disassembly of every new word. No original game bytes are stored here: only addresses, instruction text,
a hash, and the words of our own patches. Speed words are filled in by the tool ({speed}, {fast}).
Public 60 fps codes (GBAtemp, Foxes 2026) were not read or copied; sites come from the symbol-map names.
title: Fire Emblem Fates - Special Edition (USA)

speed.allowed_note: percent of the game's normal battle speed; fast-forward becomes twice that

extras.name: 60 fps battles (Fates port extra)
extras.summary: Battles (and class-change / job-intro scenes) draw 60 pictures a second instead of 30, at the same speed: the game moves battle animations by the time that passed, and the three clocks that counted game frames instead (hit-stop, slow-motion periods, the zoom-in / zoom-out camera) are switched to count time too.
extras.how: GameTime::ResetFrameStep(n) 0x004EBB38 stores n as the minimum, current and maximum number of vertical blanks per game frame (GameTime+0x10/+0x18/+0x14 = 0x006DCA94/9C/98). Graphics::WaitVSync 0x00106150 waits until that many have passed, and SceneSystem::GetDeltaTime 0x001A3858 / BattleUnit::GetTimeRate 0x0050527C scale animation by the same step. map::World::Setup and the castle pass 1 (60 fps); BattleSeq::Initialize and BattleUtil::BattleInitialize pass 2 (30 fps): the patch makes both pass 1. Three battle clocks add a fixed amount per game frame and would run twice as fast: TimeController::Tick's hit-stop (+0x18) and slow-motion periods (node +0x10) subtract the rate, TransitionCamera::Tick adds 1.0 to the encounter / comeback camera time (+0xBC). Each now goes through a small routine in the spare bytes after the code that scales the amount by step / 2 (the same as before at 30 fps).

sites.what: argument of the first call, bl GameTime::ResetFrameStep
argument of bl GameTime::ResetFrameStep (ProcJobIntro, class change)
s0 -= s16 * step / 2: a TimeController count-down in vertical blanks instead of game frames
hit-stop (freeze) count-down: freeze -= rate, now rate * step / 2
slow-motion period count-down: period -= rate, now rate * step / 2
s0 += step / 2: the battle zoom-in / zoom-out camera's clock in vertical blanks instead of game frames
the encounter / comeback camera time: time += 1.0 per game frame, now step / 2

extras.name: 60 fps story scenes (Fates port extra, test)
extras.summary: TEST ONLY, not recommended: 3D story scenes (CutSceneMain) and the title screen draw 60 pictures a second. The scenes keep their length, but the robot saw the game's random generator and the units' hidden random values come out different after a scene (docs/EXTRAS.md).
extras.how: CutSceneMain::CutSceneMain and Title::Create call GameTime::ResetFrameStep(2); the patch passes 1, as map::World::Setup does.

extras.name: Faster battles {speed}% (Fates port extra)
extras.summary: Battle animations play at {speed}% of their normal speed. Fast-forward (hold A, or the >> button) plays at twice that; slow motion (hold Y) and pause (B, or the pause button) stay as they are. Battle results do not change.
extras.how: TimeController::Tick 0x001D5CAC asks TimerButtonController::GetSelected which battle button is held and sets the world time rate (+0x24): 2 = 0.5 (slow), 3 = 0 (pause), 4 = 2.0 (fast), anything else 1.0. SceneSystem::SetTimeRate then scales every battle animation. The ten words that pick the rate are rewritten: the normal rate comes from a word inside the block ({speed}/100), fast-forward from the next one (twice that); slow motion still loads the game's own 0.5 at 0x001D5F18 and pause still uses s17 (0.0). The block ends by storing the rate exactly where the original's cases did (0x001D5DC0).

sites.what: the rate pick after bl TimerButtonController::GetSelected (10 words)

extras.name: 16:9 top screen (Fates port extra)
extras.summary: 3D scenes (map, battles) are drawn with a 16:9 camera, to go with Zakuro's top screen shape 16:9 (Settings for this game). Menus, portraits and text stay as the game draws them and are stretched by Zakuro.
extras.how: ICamera::UpdateProj 0x004DADD4 (also reached from FieldCamera::UpdateProj, the map camera) and ICamera::UpdateStereo 0x004DB474 build the top-screen projection with nn::math MTX44PerspectiveRadC_FAST(out, fovy, aspect, near, far). The camera aspect is 5:3 (400/240; ICamera::ICamera, ICamera::Reset, CameraParam). Both calls go through a small routine in the spare bytes after the code: when the aspect is exactly 5:3 it is multiplied by 16/15 (5:3 -> 16:9), then the original function runs. Other aspects (the bottom screen's 4:3, render targets) are left alone.

sites.what: the perspective case's call (s0-s3 = fovy, aspect, near, far from the camera +0x28)
